# INTERIM REPORT OF GRAM-POSITIVE COCCI IN PAIRS AND CHAINS

If chains are reported, streptococci are likely. If short chains are reported, enterococci are likely. Beta-lactam antimicrobials are more effective than vancomycin in killing susceptible streptococci and enterococci, so penicillin or ampicillin should be used if resistance is unlikely.

If the patient is severely ill or is likely to be colonized with resistant organisms, treat with vancomycin until susceptibility results are known.

References

- Medical Letter Choice of Antimicrobials 2010, 8.94

For patients with non-severe penicillin allergy
[Ceftriaxone 2 gm IV q24h \(Cost $\) M](psjizid-ceftriaxone-2gm-iv-q24h)

For patients with severe-penicillin allergy
[Vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h \(Cost $\) R](orz-set-abx-vanco-new-start-15mg-kg-q12h-mrsa-nares-screening)

## Empirical treatment of suspected enterococcal infection

[Ampicillin 2 gm IV q4h \(Cost $$\) R](psjizid-ampicillin-2-gm-iv-q4h)
